title: Your Chrome
off: Let Her open sites that need your sign-ins in your own Chrome, on the Mac Her runs on.
on: Sites that need your accounts open in your Chrome.
ready: The extension is connected, but Her doesn't use it yet.
lost: The extension is not connected. Check that Chrome is open on the Mac Her runs on, and that Hermesh is on in its extensions page.
refused: Hermesh was just updated; the extension is moving to the new version and will connect in a few seconds.
refusedStuck: The extension is still running the old program. Click its reload button on Chrome's extensions page.

outdated.extension: The extension in {{name}} is too old. It updates by itself; to update it now, choose “Update extension” in its menu.
outdated.her: The extension is newer than this Hermesh; update Hermesh on the Mac Her runs on.

guide.title: Connect Your Chrome
guide.store: Add the Hermesh extension to Chrome on the Mac Her runs on. You only do this once.
guide.install: Add the Hermesh extension to Chrome on the Mac Her runs on. You only do this once:

howto.open: In Chrome, open the extensions page:
howto.developer: Turn on “Developer mode” at the top right of the page, and leave it on: Chrome may turn the extension off without it.
howto.load: Click “Load unpacked” and choose the extension's folder in Hermesh's source:

guide.already: Added it before? Find Hermesh on the extensions page and click its reload button.
guide.waiting: Waiting for the extension in Chrome to connect…
guide.waitHint: Still not connected? Check that Chrome is open, then on its extensions page find Hermesh, make sure its switch is on, and click its reload button.
guide.doneHint: Sites that need your accounts now open in your Chrome, in every conversation from its next step. Turn it off here at any time; closing the “debugging” bar at the top of Chrome also takes a tab back.
